hasPart.description: Lots of things can cause hip pain. Common causes include a sprain, strain or arthritis. Sometimes it can be something serious like a hip fracture.

hasPart.text:
There are lots of possible causes of hip pain. It might be caused by a sudden injury or a longer-lasting problem such as arthritis.

Do not try to diagnose the cause of the pain yourself.

hasPart.headline: Causes of hip pain
See a GP if:
hasPart.text:
• hip pain is stopping you doing normal activities or affecting your sleep
  • the pain is getting worse or keeps coming back
  • the pain has not improved after treating it at home for 2 weeks
  • you have hip stiffness for more than 30 minutes after waking up
Information:

Refer yourself for back or joint help

In many areas you may be able to get help, such as physiotherapy, from NHS community musculoskeletal (MSK) services without needing a referral from a GP.

Get NHS help for back or joint problems

hasPart.headline: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
hasPart.text:
• you have severe hip pain that started suddenly but you've not had a fall or injured your hip
  • your hip is swollen and feels hot
  • the skin around your hip has changed colour
  • you have hip pain, feel generally unwell and have a high temperature (or feel hot, cold or shivery)

You can call 111 or get help from 111 online .

hasPart.headline: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
hasPart.text:
• you have severe hip pain after a fall or injury
  • you're unable to walk or put weight on your leg
  • you have any tingling or loss of feeling in your hip or leg after an injury
Find your nearest A&E

hasPart.headline: A&E safety messaging
hasPart.text:
Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

Bring any medicines you take with you.

hasPart.description: To ease hip pain, it can help to avoid putting too much strain on your hip, take painkillers, do gentle hip stretches and avoid carrying heavy things.

hasPart.text: There are things you can do to help ease hip pain.

hasPart.headline: Do
hasPart.text:
• try to avoid putting too much strain on your hip – it's best to keep moving if you can, but try not to overdo things

  • put an ice pack (or bag of frozen peas) in a towel on the painful area for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours

  • use painkillers such as paracetamol or ibuprofen gel (or ibuprofen tablets if needed)

  • wear comfortable, shock-absorbing shoes with a soft sole

  • try to lose weight if you're overweight

  • try gentle hip stretching exercises

hasPart.headline: Don't
hasPart.text:
• do not carry anything heavy

  • do not sit in low chairs – this can put extra pressure on your hips

hasPart.headline: How you can ease hip pain

hasPart.description: Treatment for hip pain depends on the cause. You may recommended strong painkillers and exercises. Some people may need hip replacement surgery.

hasPart.text:
Treatment for hip pain depends on what's causing it.

Treatments can include:

  • strong painkillers
  • simple exercises to try
  • physiotherapy for more help with exercises and stretches to ease the pain
  • occupational therapy – an occupational therapist can help with things to make your life easier, such as walking sticks or walking aids
  • steroid injections to help ease pain in your hip
  • referral to a specialist who may do a scan and discuss treatments such as surgery

Some people with pain caused by a damaged hip joint may eventually need a hip replacement if other treatments do not help.

hasPart.headline: Treatments for hip pain

hasPart.description: Hip pain is common. There are things you can do to ease the pain, but get medical help if your hip is very painful or the pain does not get better.

hasPart.text: Lots of things can cause hip pain. Common causes include a sprain, strain or arthritis. Sometimes it can be something serious like a hip fracture.
To ease hip pain, it can help to avoid putting too much strain on your hip, take painkillers, do gentle hip stretches and avoid carrying heavy things.
Treatment for hip pain depends on the cause. You may recommended strong painkillers and exercises. Some people may need hip replacement surgery.

sections.heading: Causes of hip pain
sections.text:
Causes of hip pain
There are lots of possible causes of hip pain. It might be caused by a sudden injury or a longer-lasting problem such as arthritis.
Do not try to diagnose the cause of the pain yourself.
Common causes of hip pain
Symptoms
Possible cause
Severe pain and unable to walk after a fall or injury
Hip fracture
Pain, swelling or bruising after intense or repetitive exercise
Sprain or strain, or tendonitis
Over 45 years of age, pain worse when walking and stiffness after moving
Osteoarthritis
Pain and stiffness worse after not moving (for example, when you wake up)
Rheumatoid arthritis
Hot, swollen hip and a high temperature (or feeling hot, cold or shivery)
Joint infection (septic arthritis)
Pain that may spread to your upper leg (thigh) and may feel worse when moving or lying or your side
Bursitis

headings.text: How you can ease hip pain

sections.text:
How you can ease hip pain
There are things you can do to help ease hip pain.
Do
try to avoid putting too much strain on your hip – it's best to keep moving if you can, but try not to overdo things
put an ice pack (or bag of frozen peas) in a towel on the painful area for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours
use painkillers such as
paracetamol
or
ibuprofen gel
(or ibuprofen tablets if needed)
wear comfortable, shock-absorbing shoes with a soft sole
try to lose weight if you're overweight
try gentle hip stretching exercises
Don’t
do not carry anything heavy
do not sit in low chairs – this can put extra pressure on your hips

sections.heading: Treatments for hip pain
sections.text:
Treatments for hip pain
Treatment for hip pain depends on what's causing it.
Treatments can include:
strong painkillers
simple exercises to try
physiotherapy
for more help with exercises and stretches to ease the pain
occupational therapy
– an occupational therapist can help with things to make your life easier, such as walking sticks or walking aids
steroid injections
to help ease pain in your hip
referral to a specialist who may do a scan and discuss treatments such as surgery
Some people with pain caused by a damaged hip joint may eventually need a
hip replacement
if other treatments do not help.
